newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan unions expect salary decision Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan unions expect salary decision Thursday.

text.p: Venezuelan union officials expect business leaders to provide a concrete response to their demands for higher wages Thursday following a 12-hour national work stoppage, a top union official said.
Business, government and union leaders are due to meet Thursday to discuss how to settle the wage dispute which has provoked Venezuela's first national strike in eight years.

"We need and expect a concrete reply from the business leaders in the tripartite meeting tomorrow," Carlos Navarro, secretary general of the Venezuelan Workers Confederation (CTV) told Radio Caracas Radio.
Unions claim that private companies have backed down on a commitment to raise wages made in an agreement to reform Venezuela's social security system.
The unions have received considerable support from the government, which has said that the strike is justified and salaries must be increased.
Business sector leaders, meanwhile, have said that 90 percent of businesses have raised wages.
